items.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019
items.q: he was using the quintet. It was Rusty Jones, Andy Simpkins, Billy Rodgers the guitar player from Omaha, myself and George.

ctx.x: So I think the guitar player played, when he wrote the music it came down. And I was playing with the piano and the guitar player, I believe that was an error in the beginning that became a sound and he milked it for a zillion years and it was a very cool thing. And he’s just a — I mean people call it “polite jazz.” During the height of his career he was criticized for being polite. It was too packaged. It was so, almost sweet. But this guy, I could tell you in simple terms, this guy could really play, and had an…
piano, the guitar and the vibes. And we all danced around each other like contrapuntal music —
